chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams), peace be upon them, that he was asked about a slave who slandered his wife.
He said: 'They both curse each other (perform li'an) just as the free men curse each other.'

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the two (referring to the 5th or 6th Imam)
key_terms.الْحُرَّانِ: The two free men (dual of free person)
key_terms.قَذَفَ: To slander or charge with zina (adultery/fornication)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a slave who performs li'an with his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the procedural mechanics of li'an (mutual cursing) for a slave are identical to those of a free man, emphasizing the universality of the ritual regardless of social status. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the core evidentiary function of li'an remains consistent across classes, even if subsequent legal consequences regarding manumission or fines may differ. This ruling underscores the practical application of Quranic principles in personal status law within the early Shia scholarly tradition.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having been asked about a slave having slandered his wife.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They would both curse just as the free ones curse’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked one of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about the case of a slave who accuses his woman.
He (the Imam) said, ‘They can go through the process of al-Li‘an (condemnation) against each other like free people do.””
